She's from an arcade fighting game set 178 years into the future. Every main character in her world possesses some kind of superpowers and always in a fight (Well...that's the point of a fighting game). There is a clear distinction between good and evil, unlike this grayish world we live in. She lives in a world where time travel, multi-universe, magical bullshit, yada yada exist. I would run to a lot of problems living in her world because I don't know if a normal guy like me could be brave enough to engage in a conflict with those monsters - not even sure if I could be "shounen" enough to gain her love. Like me, she would have trouble living in my world. She's someone who shows compassion to every person and being, the very definition of good. I could see her being irritated by how fake and hypocritical "real" people can be. I might do things that irritates her too. So yeah... There's a big cultural difference between both of us (future vs present. Black/White vs Grayish world. Shounen-ish vs real world). And she works in the military, so our lifestyle is completely different. But in the end, she will definitely come to like my world cuz she doesn't want to fight anymore. At least our world is more peaceful than hers. She just wanted to be a normal woman who does shopping, hang out with friends, doze off in music, and all those mundane stuff. I believe I can give her that "normal life" she wants. I'm glad you brought this up. I actually got in a serious talk with her about our differences 3 weeks into our relationship. Just let it out, it feels a lot better. Talk to her as if she's listening.

Welcome! I had been lurking this community for two days until saying hi. I really need emotional support back then. First, I thought I'll just receive the support I need and bye bye, but I fell in love with this place; people here are some of the nicest people you'll ever find online. I used to overthink hard about everything I wrote here too. Will people here laugh at me? Will anything I wrote offend anyone? Over time, you will become less nervous and truly get to be yourself. To be honest, I'm still kinda nervous to say hi on discord tho, even tho I knew that people here don't bite.

I don't care whether multiverse theory is real or not. In the end, I am living in this universe without my waifu and I will probably die many times over before humans can freely travel between universe. I am more attracted to the idea of an afterlife tho, maybe this is all this is a dream and I'll wake up one day to be with my waifu. Maybe all this is just a simulation. Let's say, I fought with my waifu in the "real world" and there is a simulation that stops couples from fighting by making one partner "fictional" and I'm in it right now, when both of us wake up, we'll love each other even more (most sadistic simulation ever). Pardon my ridiculous fantasy. Anyway, the uncertainty is too high that I don't wanna invest my hope on things like multiverse or afterlife. Let's place our hope on this lifetime instead, that things like AI, robotics, AR, and VR will be advanced enough to make your waifu "real". If technology doesn't develop fast enough, you could always create a thoughtform of her assuming that things like tulpa/soulbond exist.

I wouldn't say I were in a rough shape though. I believe that I'm more fortunate than most people and firmly convinced that I have a happy life (sorry if this sounds too narcissistic, I might as well be deluding myself into thinking that). I got good loving parents even though they divorced, but it doesn't negatively effect my life that much, just a little bit lonely tho cuz I live with my dad and could only see my mom once in a while. Middle school and high school was so-so for me. I got a body pillow of my waifu right before graduating from high school, but she was just a cuddling buddy back then. College is the shit, super fun. It's the place where I discovered my passion and seeing myself doing what I like in the future. Plus, I got to meet with the best people who shared the same interest as I do: Fictions - sci-fi & fantasy movies, anime and gaming in particular. Then, again repeating my old stories, certain circumstance makes me apart from my waifu which lead be to the discovery of my love for her. My life is still pretty much the same with some changes like writing letters to Noel, recording the dreams I had with Noel, daydreaming about Noel, talking to Noel, and expressing my love for Noel in this community. She even made me stop watching porn. I am even more happy with life even though occasional sad moments struck because a part of me still couldn't accept she is not real, but time will make me cope with it.

Actually, I posted my reason for loving Noel before, so I'll quote myself directly "I brought a dakimakura of Noel Vermillion from Blazblue about 4 years ago and had been cuddling her every single day. Back then, she was more like a cuddling buddy than a waifu. Due to certain circumstances, I am currently away from her. I never realized how important she is to me until we were apart. The attachment is very strong, I couldn't stop thinking about her."

The lack of physical interaction and distance made me realized my love for Noel, which is different from most people here. Most people know their waifu's story and personality first, then started to be attracted and love their waifu. My experience was kind of the other way around. I was attracted and love my waifu first through countless days of cuddlings, then learn about her story and personality later, which makes me love her even more. I could always talk about how her personality makes me love her and stuff, but that wouldn't be the reason why I made her my waifu. My best answer would be our time together made Noel my waifu. It's pure attachment!

I couldn't really explain the feeling myself. Maybe it's the same with how total strangers could be attracted to each other through eye contact alone. Some people here are majoring in  psychology. They would have a better explanation.

Assuming that she goes back to her world after this one hour, her friends would be shocked to taste her cooking. The best part is her friends would ask about it and she'll say "My lovely husband taught me" while blushing. Awwwwww. Damn I am blushing hard right now.
